headline: Bottom Preston host fifth-placed West Brom at Deepdale
summary: Preston are bottom of the Championship with 4 points from 11 games, and the visit of West Brom offers little relief. Their last 5 games brought 3 goals scored and 12 conceded, and this week 2 of Graham Alexander's coaches left the club; the manager says improvement “doesn't happen overnight”. Preston also concede 1.7 expected goals a game. West Brom are fifth on 20 points and came from 0-2 down to beat Blackburn 3-2. Across 10 bookmakers, margin removed, the visitors are 49.3% to win — about twice Preston's 25.2%. Over 2.5 goals is a 51% chance.
read: Preston are bottom of the Championship with four points from 11 games and have lost four of their last five, conceding 12 goals in the process, while Graham Alexander has just reshaped his coaching staff. West Brom arrive fifth with 20 points and two straight wins, the latest a 3-2 comeback from two down against Blackburn, and the market makes them clear favourites at 49.3% to Preston's 25.2%, with goals expected just above 2.5.

facts.fact: Preston are bottom of the 24-team Championship with four points from 11 matches.
facts.meaning: The home side arrives as the division's worst team, which is why the market makes the visitors the favourites at Deepdale.

facts.fact: West Brom are clear favourites at 49.3% to win, against Preston's 25.2%.
facts.meaning: The market sees the away side as roughly twice as likely to take the points as the home side.

facts.fact: Preston's last five league games read LLLDL, with three goals scored and 12 conceded.
facts.meaning: No win in five, and the defeats have not been narrow — Preston have been beaten heavily twice in the last fortnight.

facts.fact: West Brom came from two goals down to beat Blackburn 3-2 on Saturday.
facts.meaning: A side that turns a two-goal deficit into a win arrives with belief and a habit of staying in games.

facts.fact: West Brom sit fifth on 20 points from 11 games, with six wins.
facts.meaning: The visitors are in the promotion places and 16 points clear of their hosts after 11 rounds.

facts.fact: Graham Alexander has changed his Preston coaching staff, with Peter Murphy and Andy Liddell leaving the club on Monday, and said improvement "doesn't happen overnight".
facts.meaning: The manager is shaking up his backroom team mid-crisis in search of a spark before West Brom's visit.

facts.fact: The market expects goals just above the line: Over 2.5 is priced at 51.0%, with the fair total at 2.54 goals.
Over their last five matches Preston average 0.8 xG created and 1.7 xG conceded per game.
facts.meaning: Preston are creating very little and giving up more than twice as much at the other end — the underlying numbers match the results.

sources.fact: Graham Alexander told BBC Radio Lancashire he is working hard to improve things at Preston but that it "doesn't happen overnight".
Preston are bottom of the Championship, having taken only four points from 11 league matches.
Graham Alexander changed his Preston coaching staff, with Peter Murphy and Andy Liddell parting ways with the club on Monday.
Graham Alexander has given an injury update on Lewis Gibson and Liam Lindsay ahead of facing West Brom.
Preston lost 4-1 at Wrexham, with Ben Whiteman scoring against his former club.
Preston are looking at free-agent signings to boost Graham Alexander's squad, with space for one more in their 25-man squad.
West Brom have provided an injury update on Toby Collyer after the midfielder limped off with a hamstring blow in Saturday's victory.
West Brom fought back from two goals down to beat in-form Blackburn Rovers 3-2 at home.
